extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys and IP practitioners prosecuting European patents (and litigating in Germany)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and case-law-based standards for how and to what extent a European patent application/patent description must be adapted when the claims are amended (deleting or marking embodiments, clarity/support interplay, and practical implications before EPO and German courts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistencies between the description and the claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inconsistency between the description and the claims must be avoided if it may throw doubt on the extent of protection and therefore render the claim unclear or unsupported under Art. 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes simple verbal inconsistencies and inconsistencies regarding apparently essential features not mentioned in the independent claims, as well as cases where part of the subject-matter of the description and/or drawings is not covered by the claims. The EPO Guidelines (F‑IV, 4.3) expect such inconsistencies to be removed or remedied so as not to create doubt about claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default deletion of embodiments not covered by independent claims (March 2021 approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Embodiments in the description which are no longer covered by the independent claims must be deleted (…) unless these embodiments can reasonably be considered to be useful for highlighting specific aspects of the amended claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The March 2021 EPO Guidelines required, as a general rule, deletion of inconsistent embodiments; retaining them was an exception only if they legitimately help to highlight aspects of the amended claims. This strict approach is traceable to earlier Board decisions (e.g., T 1808/06).

rubrics_metrics.name: When retaining inconsistent embodiments, they must be clearly and specifically marked (March 2022 requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If inconsistent embodiments are not deleted, the fact that an embodiment is not covered by the claims must be prominently stated and must refer to one or more specific embodiments using unambiguous expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The March 2022 Guidelines leave the choice to applicants whether to delete or mark inconsistent embodiments, but impose conditions for marking: statements must explicitly and unambiguously identify specific embodiments as not falling within the claimed subject-matter. Generic statements at the description start are insufficient; merely replacing terms like "embodiment" or "invention" with "example" or "disclosure" is not enough. Mandatory features of an independent claim may not be presented as optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic disclaimers or superficial edits are insufficient to avoid inconsistency
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not sufficient to make a generic statement that 'embodiments not falling under the scope of the (…) claims are to be considered merely as examples', nor is it sufficient only to replace terms such as 'embodiment' or 'invention' by 'example' or 'disclosure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use unambiguous, specific statements referring to particular embodiments when marking them as not covered; otherwise examiners/boards may consider the description inconsistent with the claims and require deletion or amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be clear in themselves; the description cannot be relied on to resolve clarity issues (T 1989/18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 84 EPC requires that the claims are clear, i.e. properly define and delimit the subject-matter for which protection is sought in understandable and unambiguous terms. Claims must be clear in themselves when read with normal skills including knowledge about the prior art, but not including any knowledge derived from the description of the application or the amended patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this view (Board decision T 1989/18), the description cannot be used to resolve a clarity issue in a claim, nor can it give rise to such an issue if the claim is clear per se. Support (that the claimed subject-matter is described) remains relevant, but clarity assessment should not import descriptive material to make claims clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support requirement entails that the entire description should be consistent with the claims (T 1024/18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement in Article 84 EPC of the claims to be supported by the description includes that the description is consistent with the claims not only in some part but throughout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: According to decision T 1024/18, longstanding Boards' case law requires consistency between the entirety of the description and the claims; embodiments inconsistent with the claims must therefore be deleted or clearly identifiable to the reader. This decision explicitly contradicts the T 1989/18 approach on this point and aligns with the March 2022 EPO Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical expectation: EPO examiners will generally follow the Guidelines despite divergent Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if there are diverging decisions of Boards of Appeal, EPO examiners will, generally speaking, follow the common practice as described in the EPO Guidelines (EPO Guidelines, General Part, section 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Guidelines were revised (March 2022) to relax deletion in favour of allowing marking under strict conditions, applicants should expect examiners to enforce the Guidelines' current text, and thus to require deletion or appropriate marking per the specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to adapt the description can lead to refusal even if claims are otherwise grantable
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be refused where the description contains passages referring to 'embodiments of the invention' which contain subject-matter not covered by an allowable independent claim, and the applicant does not agree to amend the description as requested (Article 84 objection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical case: Examining Division refused application no. 12 810 245.6 on this ground — showing the procedural risk if applicants refuse to delete or properly mark inconsistent embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: German litigation practice: keep original disclosure and add explicit indications when parts are no longer covered
rubrics_metrics.description: For enforcement of an EP patent before German courts, it is in the interest of applicants to ensure that patent descriptions comprise all text as filed and to add indications that certain parts of the original disclosure are no longer covered by the granted claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under German patent law the description and drawings form the basis for claim construction and file history is not available; German courts tend to consider all originally disclosed embodiments as useful for highlighting aspects of amended claims. Therefore, marking specific parts as not covered (rather than deleting them) is recommended to help courts understand the patentee's and EPO's views on relevance and prior art.
